key_insight: A frozen time-series reconstructor can impute a missing sensor channel by optimizing missing inputs at test time to improve reconstruction consistency on observed channels.
engineering_relevance: This offers a way to adapt existing reconstruction models to sensor-channel failures without retraining, at the cost of substantially slower inference.
method: Train a sequence reconstructor without artificial mask augmentation, then freeze its weights.
Optimize missing entries through the frozen model while clamping observations and minimizing observed-coordinate reconstruction error.
Assess missing-to-observed coupling via the cross-Jacobian; optionally add a temporal-smoothness prior when coupling is weak.
evidence_signal: Across five real-world datasets and four architectures with one synthetically missing channel per test window, no-prior refinement reduced MAE versus one-pass reconstruction in 19 of 20 combinations; the best refined reconstructor beat mask-aware baselines on two datasets but trailed on three.
watch_item: Benefits depend on cross-channel coupling, and evaluation with exactly one missing channel does not establish performance under simultaneous channel failures.
paper_title: From Reconstruction to Imputation: Test-Time Optimization for Missing Time-Series Channels
